questions.q: What SQL Server tool does pg_stat_statements serve the same purpose as, per this lesson?
options: Query Store
SQL Server Profiler traces only
The buffer pool
RESTORE LOG
questions.explain: Both track execution statistics for queries running on the server so a DBA can find worst offenders with data instead of guessing.

questions.q: Why does enabling pg_stat_statements require a server restart?
options: It must be listed in shared_preload_libraries, which is only read at server start
It rewrites the entire data directory
It requires a new PostgreSQL major version
It can only be enabled during initial cluster creation
questions.explain: shared_preload_libraries is only read when PostgreSQL starts, so adding pg_stat_statements to it requires a restart before CREATE EXTENSION can activate it.

questions.q: How does pg_stat_statements aggregate queries with different literal parameter values, like WHERE id = 5 and WHERE id = 12?
options: It normalizes the query text and tracks them as the same entry
It creates a separate row for every distinct literal value
It ignores queries containing literals entirely
It only tracks the most recent execution of each literal
questions.explain: Normalized query text strips out literal values, so structurally identical queries are aggregated together into one entry.

questions.q: Sorting pg_stat_statements by total_exec_time finds what, per this lesson?
options: Queries costing the most cumulative server time overall, not necessarily the slowest single execution
Only queries that have never been executed
The queries with the fewest total calls
Queries sorted alphabetically by query text
questions.explain: A query run very frequently even at low per-call cost can outrank a rarely-run slow query in total cumulative time.

questions.q: What does mean_exec_time help you find that total_exec_time does not, per this lesson?
options: Individually slow queries, regardless of how often they run
The number of rows in a table
Which extension is currently loaded
The current WAL archiving status
questions.explain: mean_exec_time is average time per call, surfacing queries that are slow on a per-execution basis even if they don't run often.
